learning_outcomes.text: Face the complete implementation of an “embedded system” based on microprocessors and/or microcontrollers in their professional life.
Fluently handle the datasheets of typical electronic components of embedded systems: microprocessors, microcontrollers, and peripheral integrated circuits.

Understand the characteristics of microcontrollers, establish their field of application, and select the most suitable microcontroller for a given application, from a technical and economic point of view.
Know the programming language for a specific microprocessor/microcontroller, and use the most common development tools: assembler, compilers, simulators, emulators, etc., that facilitate development.
Work in a group, reason critically to compare different solutions, and discriminate the most optimal one.
Acquire the ability to solve open problems and projects through analysis and information search. Defend their solution against other possible ones through oral communication.
Use A/D and D/A conversion circuits, both discrete and integrated into microcontrollers or other devices.
Design and implement digital systems using timer blocks, A/D and D/A converters integrated into microcontrollers, and select the optimal one for each application.
Know and use the most common digital communication buses and standards between systems (RS-232, RS-485, etc.) and between integrated circuits (SPI, I2C, etc.).
Manage and design complex I/O circuits and interfaces, such as LCDs and their associated circuits, both at a logical and electrical level.
Include basic signal processing and control algorithms in the design, selecting the most appropriate in each case, according to technical and economic criteria.
Know the different design strategies in microelectronics.
Have a global vision of digital design, and be able to evaluate the use of different available resources to address it, from a technical-economic point of view, given certain specifications.

assessment_rules: To pass the course in the ordinary session, a minimum score of 5 out of 10 must be obtained in the theoretical exam (T1). If this minimum is not met, or if the student wishes to retake the exam, it can be done in the official call's theoretical exam. The final grade is calculated as (0.95 * (0.5 * (P1 + T1))) + (0.05 * PA), provided all minimums are met. Otherwise, the grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. In the extraordinary session, only a theoretical exam covering all theoretical content is evaluated, and its score is the final grade.
